name: Jordan Lee
summary: Product data analyst with seven years in analytics. For the last four and a half years I have worked at a B2B payroll and time-tracking software company whose customers have 5 to 200 employees. I study churn and retention with Python and SQL and present the results to the product team and to company leadership.

bullets: Built a churn model (Python, pandas, scikit-learn) that flags small-business accounts likely to cancel in the next 60 days. Customer Success calls the top 200 accounts on the list each month.
Presented churn drivers to the CEO, CFO and VP of Product at the 2024 planning offsite. Pricing for the time-tracking add-on changed afterwards.

Analysed retention for the time-tracking add-on and found that accounts which connected their scheduling tool in week one had 90-day retention 18 points higher. The onboarding flow was changed to prompt that step.
Ran a six-week A/B test of the onboarding checklist on about 4,000 new accounts, and the variant raised week-one activation from 41% to 47%.
Created the account health score that Customer Success uses. It combines weighted product-usage signals, and an Airflow job refreshes it daily.
Replaced the finance team's hand-updated spreadsheets with SQL transformations in Snowflake, scheduled in Airflow. Wrote a data dictionary for the 60 core tables.
Defined Segment event tracking with product managers for new features before launch.
Reviewed the other two analysts' SQL and Python in GitHub pull requests, about five a week.
Mentored a junior analyst on survival analysis of churn (Kaplan-Meier curves and a Cox model in the lifelines library).
Built and maintained Tableau dashboards for the product team and presented the quarterly retention review to the VP of Product.
Automated the weekly loan-pipeline report with SQL and Power BI. Preparation time fell from about six hours to under one.
Supported the lending team's monthly reporting in SQL Server and Excel.
